10,000-row fit validation

Source: vignettes/articles/legacy-fit-validation.Rmd
legacy-fit-validation.Rmd

Scope

On 2026-10-18, the two-dimensional trapezoid-exponential example was fitted through both emhawkes::hfit() and frpp::ffit(). This checks compatibility of the existing bridge, rather than a new independent estimation engine.

Both simulations used seed 1107 and produced exactly the same data and final RNG state: 10,000 rows including the initial row, or 9,999 events. Initial components were zero. The six shared parameters were mu1, alpha1.1, alpha1.2, beta1.1, a and ell; residual parameters were estimated jointly. Both fits used the same density-domain validator, nonnegative constraints, a <= 3, maxLik BFGS and control = list(iterlim = 1000, reltol = 1e-8).

The environment was Windows, R 4.5.1, emhawkes 1.0.1 and maxLik 1.5-2.1. The fitting comparison used emhawkes without the unreleased shared-kernel API.

Results

Across three paired repetitions, coefficients, reported log likelihoods, initial-state arguments and the underlying optimizer Hessians matched exactly. Both interfaces returned optimizer code 0. Fitting did not consume RNG state. The reported log likelihood was -12411.1075525012. Restored models reproduced it with zero difference.

Shared parameter Estimate, identical in both interfaces
mu1 0.3037481375
alpha1.1 0.5422426583
alpha1.2 0.8534686090
beta1.1 1.5996890464
a 0.7243553975
ell 1.6487607808

A separate fresh-session check reloaded all six fits and compared their restored bridge inference with the experimental shared-kernel backend. The maximum absolute log-likelihood difference was 1.13e-10; full inference outputs passed the existing relative comparison tolerance of 1e-10. This additional check requires the emhawkes development API.

Using the same precomputed interval values, the bridge’s separate accumulated sums and the state’s event-wise accumulated sum exactly reproduced their respective likelihoods. Summation order alone explains the entire difference; no state value or comparison tolerance was changed. The optional replay script also checks and records this calculation.

Standard errors

The shared optimizer Hessian was indefinite: the minimum eigenvalue of its negative was -9402.647211. The stored maximum absolute score was 5.672282; optimizer code 0 alone does not establish a well-resolved optimum.

The original provider produced nonfinite standard errors for a and ell. ffit() reported wald = "unavailable" and reason = "nonpositive_curvature", withholding the full free-parameter Wald covariance. The raw Hessian matched the original calculation; it was not repaired or replaced. Finite errors for the other four parameters in the original output do not validate an indefinite information matrix.

These checks establish matching estimation behavior on this dataset. They do not prove a global optimum or confidence-interval coverage. FRPP-specific profile likelihood and bootstrap inference remain separate work.

Elapsed fitting time

The two public likelihood routes were evaluated three times before timing. The full fitting calls were then timed sequentially in alternating order: hfit/ffit, ffit/hfit, hfit/ffit. Package loading, simulation, likelihood warm-up and post-fit replay were excluded. No package builds or checks ran alongside these measurements. Times include each public fitting call and its result construction. These are three repetitions on one dataset, not a speed claim for other FRPP models.

Interface Median seconds Range, seconds
hfit 332.01 331.81–334.19
ffit 340.95 336.81–341.84

Reproduce

From the frpp repository with both packages installed:

Rscript tools/validate-legacy-fit.R results/legacy-fit 3

With the emhawkes development shared-kernel API installed, also run:

Rscript tools/replay-fit-validation.R results/legacy-fit

The script saves inputs, fits, coefficients, convergence and curvature summaries, comparisons, elapsed times and session information. It stops on a comparison failure; it does not widen the fixed tolerance. The FRPP examples show the new interface, and the legacy vignette retains the original code.
